_comment: Legitimate traffic that a signature set is tempting to block by accident.
Every case here must be allowed by the whole rule chain.
A false positive is not a lesser bug than a miss. A filter that blocks
O'Brien from signing in, or an article about the European Union, gets
switched off by the operator — and then it catches nothing at all. Several
of these are deliberately adversarial: they contain the exact keywords the
signatures look for, in contexts where they are harmless.
Same wire-form convention as attacks.json: 'query' is percent-encoded.

cases.description: A Spanish search term with accents and spaces
The word 'union' in an article slug — 'union' alone is not an injection
A tutorial search: SELECT and UNION both present, but in the wrong order for union_select
'javascript' without a colon is a topic, not a URI scheme
O'Brien — the canonical WAF false positive
A price filter using <, > and the word 'and'
A double dash with no quote in front of it is a dash, not a SQL comment
A real sign-in POST, password included
A product review, the same endpoint the stored-XSS vector uses
A real User-Agent, semicolons and all — headers are scanned too

headers.user-agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/131.0 Safari/537.36

cases.description: A data: URI that is not text/html
An accented question mark and a question word
An address in a POST body — the @ and the dots must not trip anything
